questions.question: Who among the following was awarded the Abel Prize 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Masaki Kashiwara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Masaki Kashiwara**, a distinguished mathematician from **Kyoto University**, was officially announced as the recipient of the **Abel Prize 2025** on **March 26, 2025**.
 
• The **Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters** awarded him for his **fundamental contributions** to **algebraic analysis** and **representation theory**, fields where he has been a visionary for over five decades.
 
• The citation particularly emphasizes his pioneering development of the **theory of D-modules** and his groundbreaking discovery of **crystal bases**, which provide an algebraic language for studying systems of **linear partial differential equations**.
 
• By receiving this honor, Kashiwara became the **first Japanese mathematician** to win the **Abel Prize** since its establishment in 2003.
 
• The award ceremony was held on **May 20, 2025**, at the **University of Oslo**, where **King Harald V** of Norway presented the prize to the laureate.
 
• His work, specifically the **Sato-Kashiwara theory**, bridges several mathematical disciplines, including **microlocal analysis**, **symplectic geometry**, and **algebraic geometry**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abel Prize Overview**:

 
 
• It was established by the **Government of Norway** in **2001** to commemorate the **200th birth anniversary** of **Niels Henrik Abel**, a legendary Norwegian mathematician.
 
• Managed by the **Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters**, it is often termed the **Nobel Prize of Mathematics** because the traditional Nobel categories do not include mathematics.
 
• The prize includes a monetary reward of **7.5 million Norwegian kroner**.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Laureates**:
 
 
• **Luis Caffarelli**: Awarded the prize in **2023** for his contributions to the **regularity theory** of **nonlinear partial differential equations**.
 
• **Avi Wigderson**: Received the prize in **2021** (shared with László Lovász) for foundational work in **theoretical computer science** and **discrete mathematics**.
 
• **Karen Uhlenbeck**: Honored in **2019**, she was the **first woman** to receive the Abel Prize for her achievements in **geometric partial differential equations** and **gauge theory**.
 
• **Michel Talagrand**: Awarded the prize in **2024** for his research in **probability theory** and **functional analysis**.

questions.question: The 2025 study detecting airborne microplastics in the mangroves of Sundarbans was done by scientists from which institute?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Microplastics** are tiny plastic particles less than 5 mm in size that pose a significant threat to global ecosystems. While aquatic and terrestrial plastic pollution is well-documented, **atmospheric transport** of these particles to remote and protected regions is a recent area of critical research. Detecting these particles in pristine environments like the **Sundarbans** signifies that even uninhabited, protected natural fortresses are no longer safe from human-induced pollution.

**Given**

 
• Year of study: **2025**
 
• Pollutant type: **Airborne microplastics**
 
• Location: **Sundarbans mangroves** (specifically the **Chula Kathi Protection Camp**)

**Calculation/Explanation**

In **January 2025**, a team of scientists conducted an intensive eight-day winter campaign in the **Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve**. Using high-volume air samplers, they detected an average of 10 ± 6 microplastic particles per 100 cubic metres of air. The study, published in the international journal **Science of the Total Environment**, provided the first evidence of atmospheric microplastics in a protected natural ecosystem in India.

The research was led by **Abhinandan Ghosh** and **Dr. Gopala Krishna Darbha** from the **Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Kolkata**. Their findings revealed that tiny **fibres** and **fragments**, predominantly made of industrial polymers like **polypropylene (PP)** and **polyethylene (PE)**, were being transported through the air from urban sources into the remote mangrove forests.

Comparing this information with the provided options:

 
• **IISER Kolkata**: The institute that conducted the study.
 
• **IIT Kharagpur**: Not the primary institute for this specific atmospheric study.
 
• **NIO Goa**: Focused on oceanography, not the lead on this airborne study in the Sundarbans.
 
• **WII Dehradun**: Focused on wildlife, not the primary authors of this environmental chemistry paper.

**Final Answer:** **IISER Kolkata**

questions.question: Who among the following was associated with the Farazi Movement in Bengal during the 19th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadu Mian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Farazi Movement** (or Faraizi Movement) was founded by **Haji Shariatullah** in **1818** in **East Bengal** to advocate for radical religious, social, and political changes within the Islamic community.
 
• **Dadu Mian** (whose real name was **Mohammad Mohsin**) was the son of Haji Shariatullah and took leadership of the movement in **1840**, significantly expanding its influence during the **19th century**.
 
• Under **Dadu Mian**, the movement shifted from pure religious reform to a powerful agrarian uprising against the exploitation of **zamindars** (landlords) and **British indigo planters**.
 
• He organized a disciplined **paramilitary force** and established a parallel government in parts of **Bengal**, popularizing the revolutionary doctrine that **land belongs to God** and therefore no tax should be paid to human masters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **U Kiang Nongbah**:

 
 
• A legendary freedom fighter from the **Jaintia Hills** (present-day **Meghalaya**).
 
• He led an armed uprising against the **British** in **1862** following the imposition of the **House Tax**.
 
 
 
• **Majnu Shah** (Maznoom Shah):
 
 
• A prominent leader of the **Fakir-Sannyasi Rebellion** that occurred in **Bengal** during the late 18th century.
 
• He led groups of wandering **Fakirs** in raids against the **British East India Company** factories and treasuries.
 
 
 
• **Birsa Munda**:
 
 
• A tribal freedom fighter and folk hero who belonged to the **Munda tribe**.
 
• He spearheaded the **Munda Rebellion** (also known as **Ulgulan** or the Great Tumult) in the **Chhota Nagpur** region between **1899 and 1900** against **British** colonial rule and the **Dikus** (outsiders).

questions.question: Which global event first initiated coordinated international action on environmental protection and development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stockholm Conference, 1972**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United Nations Conference on the Human Environment (UNCHE)**, held in **Stockholm, Sweden**, from **June 5 to June 16, 1972**, was the first global conference to make the environment a major international issue.
 
• The event was attended by representatives from **113 countries** and led to the adoption of the **Stockholm Declaration**, which established **26 principles** for environmental management and **109 recommendations** for international action.
 
• One of the primary outcomes of the summit was the creation of the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**, the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda.
 
• The conference emphasized the link between **economic development** and **environmental integrity**, laying the groundwork for the concept of **sustainable development**.
 
• To mark the start of this historic event, the **United Nations General Assembly** designated **June 5** as **World Environment Day**, which has been celebrated annually since **1973**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rio Conference, 1992**:

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Earth Summit** or **UNCED**, it took place in **Rio de Janeiro, Brazil**.
 
• It resulted in landmark agreements including **Agenda 21**, the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**, and the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**.
 
 
 
• **Johannesburg Summit, 2002**:
 
 
• Known as the **World Summit on Sustainable Development (WSSD)** or **Rio+10**, it focused on the implementation of the goals set during the **1992 Earth Summit**.
 
• Key themes included **poverty eradication**, **water sanitation**, and **sustainable energy**.
 
 
 
• **Doha Climate Meeting, 2012**:
 
 
• The **COP 18** meeting resulted in the **Doha Amendment** to the **Kyoto Protocol**, extending its commitment period until **2020**.
 
• It addressed the **Loss and Damage** mechanism for developing countries vulnerable to climate change.

questions.question: Which of the following water bodies separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten Degree Channel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ten Degree Channel** is a major water body in the **Bay of Bengal** that acts as a physical separator between the **Andaman Islands** to the north and the **Nicobar Islands** to the south.
 
• It derives its name from its geographical location on the **10° N latitude** line, which runs directly between the two island groups.
 
• The channel is approximately **150 kilometers** (93 miles) wide from north to south and is deep enough to facilitate **international shipping** and **maritime traffic**.
 
• Specifically, it separates **Little Andaman** (the southernmost island of the Andaman archipelago) from **Car Nicobar** (the northernmost island of the Nicobar archipelago).
 
• This channel is ecologically significant and serves as a vital corridor for **marine biodiversity** in the **Indian Ocean** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palk Strait**:

 
 
• It is a strait located between the **Tamil Nadu** state of **India** and the **Jaffna District** of **Sri Lanka**.
 
• It connects the **Bay of Bengal** in the northeast with the **Palk Bay** and the **Gulf of Mannar** in the southwest.
 
 
 
• **Duncan Passage**:
 
 
• This is a narrow **strait** in the **Indian Ocean**, measuring approximately **48 kilometers** (30 miles) in width.
 
• It separates **Rutland Island** (part of the Great Andaman group) to the north from **Little Andaman** to the south.
 
 
 
• **Nine Degree Channel**:
 
 
• Located in the **Arabian Sea**, it is part of the **Lakshadweep** archipelago.
 
• It separates the island of **Minicoy** from the main **Lakshadweep islands** (specifically Kalpeni and Suheli Par) and lies on the **9° N latitude**.
 
 
 
• **Eight Degree Channel**:
 
 
• This channel separates the **Minicoy Island** of India from the **Maldives**.

questions.question: According to the Sustainable Development Goals National Indicator Framework (SDG NIF) Progress Report of 2025, social protection coverage rose from 22% in 2016 to what percentage in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**64.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals − National Indicator Framework (SDG NIF) Progress Report 2025** was released by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** on **June 29, 2025**, to commemorate **National Statistics Day**.
 
• This report provides a comprehensive review of India's progress toward the **2030 Agenda** using **284 national indicators** developed in consultation with various ministries and **NITI Aayog**.
 
• Under **SDG Goal 1 (No Poverty)**, Indicator **1.3.1** tracks the **proportion of the population covered by social protection floors/systems**, which includes benefits for children, the unemployed, older persons, and the vulnerable.
 
• According to the data snapshot provided in the report, social protection coverage in India experienced a significant surge from **22.0% in 2016** to **64.3% in 2025**.
 
• This massive expansion indicates that nearly **two-thirds** of the Indian population is now receiving at least one form of social protection benefit, reflecting the government's push for inclusive growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The expansion of social protection is attributed to several large-scale government initiatives:
 
 
• **Aadhaar-linked identification**: The use of encrypted **Aadhaar** as a unique identifier allowed for a more accurate count of beneficiaries across multiple schemes.
 
• **Major Welfare Schemes**: Programs such as **MGNREGA** (employment), **PM-POSHAN** (nutrition), **Ayushman Bharat** (health), and the **e-Shram portal** for unorganized workers have significantly widened the safety net.
 
• **Global Recognition**: The **International Labour Organization (ILO)**, in its **World Social Protection Report 2024-26**, also noted that India's social protection coverage effectively doubled in the last few years.
 
• **Future Projections**: While the 2025 report recorded **64.3%**, preliminary data for the **2026 Progress Report** suggests a further increase to approximately **65.3%**.

questions.question: What is the full form of UNDP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Development Programme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** serves as the global development network for the **United Nations**, facilitating change and connecting countries to knowledge and resources.
 
• It was officially established on **November 22, 1965**, following the merger of the **Expanded Programme of Technical Assistance (EPTA)** and the **Special Fund**.
 
• Headquartered in **New York City**, the organization operates in approximately **170 countries and territories** to eradicate poverty and reduce inequalities.
 
• The **UNDP** is the primary body responsible for assisting nations in achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, also known as the **Global Goals**, by the year **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Reports (HDR)**:

 
 
• The **UNDP** is widely recognized for publishing the annual **Human Development Report**, which introduced the **Human Development Index (HDI)**.
 
• The **HDI** is a composite statistic used to rank countries by level of human development, focusing on **longevity**, **education**, and **per capita income**.
 
 
 
• **Governance and Leadership**:
 
 
• The agency is led by an **Administrator**, a position currently held by **Achim Steiner**. The Administrator is the **third highest-ranking official** in the **United Nations**.
 
• The **UNDP Executive Board**, consisting of representatives from **36 nations**, provides intergovernmental support and supervision for the activities of the organization.
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas**:
 
 
• It focuses on three main pillars: **Sustainable Development**, **Democratic Governance and Peacebuilding**, and **Climate and Disaster Resilience**.

questions.question: Which of the following musical genres was considered formal and divine in ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandharva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In ancient Indian musicology, **Gandharva** refers to a highly structured, formal, and sacred musical tradition that was believed to be of divine origin and pleasing to the gods.
 
• As detailed in the **Natyashastra** by **Bharata Muni** and the **Dattilam** by **Dattila**, this genre was defined by the strict union of three elements: **Svara** (notes), **Tala** (rhythm), and **Pada** (meaningful text).
 
• It was considered **Anadi-Nidhana** (eternal) and was categorized as **Marga** music, representing a spiritual path intended for liberation (**Moksha**) rather than mere entertainment.
 
• The name is derived from the **Gandharvas**, who are celestial beings and divine musicians in **Hindu mythology**, highlighting the genre's association with the heavens and ritualistic worship.
 
• Unlike later evolving styles, **Gandharva** music was rigid in its rules, ensuring that the sanctity and specific spiritual vibrations of the hymns were preserved through centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gana**:

 
 
• While often used as a general term for singing, in the context of ancient treatises, **Gana** referred to the broader practice of musical performance that eventually allowed for regional and creative variations, moving away from the strict **Gandharva** rituals.
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad**:
 
 
• This is one of the oldest surviving forms of **Hindustani Classical Music**, characterized by its austere and grand nature.
 
• Although it has roots in ancient Vedic chanting and **Prabandhas**, it flourished significantly later during the medieval period under patrons like **Raja Man Singh Tomar** of Gwalior and **Emperor Akbar**.
 
 
 
• **Prabandh**:
 
 
• A structured musical composition that was highly popular between the **11th and 14th centuries**.
 
• It served as a vital evolutionary link between the ancient **Gandharva** style and modern classical forms, with **Jayadeva’s Gita Govinda** being a famous example of this literary-musical structure.

questions.question: In October 2025, the Ministry of Minority Affairs announced support to universities to set up **Centres of Excellence** to promote heritage and classical languages. This initiative was taken under which scheme?

options.text: Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** announced support to several central universities in **October 2025** to establish **Centres of Excellence (CoE)** focused on promoting and preserving **heritage and classical languages**.
 
• This significant initiative is being implemented under the **Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK)**, which is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS)** designed to improve socio-economic conditions and basic amenities for minority communities.
 
• The project aims to facilitate advanced research, digitization of ancient manuscripts, and the development of specialized degree and diploma courses in languages like **Arabic**, **Persian**, **Sanskrit**, **Pali**, and **Prakrit**.
 
• Key academic institutions designated for these centres include **Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI)**, **Aligarh Muslim University (AMU)**, the **University of Delhi**, and the **Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (CIBS)** in Leh.
 
• This move is aligned with the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which emphasizes the preservation of India's **linguistic diversity** and the integration of traditional Indian knowledge systems into modern higher education.
 
• The **PMJVK** scheme, formerly known as the **Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MsDP)**, has been restructured to prioritize high-impact projects in **education**, **health**, and **skill development** within **Minority Concentration Areas (MCAs)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS)**:

 
 
• An integrated scheme focusing on the **livelihood**, **skilling**, and **entrepreneurship** of minority communities, particularly for traditional artisans and craftspersons.
 
• It converges several previous initiatives including **Seekho aur Kamao**, **USTTAD**, **Hamari Dharohar**, **Nai Roshni**, and **Nai Manzil**.
 
 
 
• **National Minorities Development Finance Corporation (NMDFC)**:
 
 
• A **Schedule C Government Company** incorporated in **1994** that provides **concessional loans** for self-employment to individuals from notified minority communities.
 
• It operates through **State Channelising Agencies (SCAs)** to provide micro-credit and educational loans.
 
 
 
• **Maulana Azad National Fellowship (MANF)**:
 
 
• A fellowship scheme that provides financial assistance to students from **notified minority communities** to pursue higher research programs like **M.Phil** and **Ph.D.** in Indian universities.

questions.question: Which approach is crucial for empowering rural women, leading to community development?

options.text: Limiting educational opportunities to urban centres

Restricting women's roles to traditional household duties
Focussing solely on men's employment programmes

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vocational training** provides rural women with specialized skills in sectors such as **agro-processing, handicrafts, textile manufacturing, and digital literacy**, facilitating their entry into the workforce.
 
• **Gender-specific education** acknowledges and addresses the unique socio-cultural barriers women face, such as **limited mobility** and domestic responsibilities, by providing **flexible learning schedules** and local training centers.
 
• Economic empowerment through skill development leads to a **multiplier effect**; women tend to reinvest a higher portion of their income into their family's **nutrition, health, and children's education**.
 
• Empowering women enables them to participate in **local governance** and decision-making bodies like **Gram Sabhas**, ensuring that community development projects are inclusive and address the needs of all demographics.
 
• By shifting from **unpaid subsistence labor** to income-generating activities, women contribute directly to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** and reduce the **poverty gap** in rural regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Women's Empowerment**:

 
 
• Defined as the process of increasing women's **self-worth** and their ability to determine their own choices and influence **social change**.
 
• It involves five core dimensions: **economic, social, political, psychological, and physical** autonomy.
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**: Often serve as the primary platform for delivering vocational training and **microfinance** to rural women.
 
 
 
• **Community Development**:
 
 
• A holistic process focused on improving the **social, economic, and environmental** conditions of a specific locality.
 
• Integration of women into the **rural economy** is a prerequisite for achieving **Sustainable Development Goal 5 (Gender Equality)** and **Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)**.

questions.question: The presence of elaborate gopurams is a defining feature of which temple architectural style?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dravidian style** of temple architecture is native to **South India** and reached its zenith under the patronage of dynasties such as the **Pallavas**, **Cholas**, **Pandyas**, and the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• The most striking feature of this style is the **Gopuram**, which is a monumental, multi-storied gateway tower decorated with intricate sculptures of deities and celestial beings.
 
• In the **Dravidian style**, the temple complex is always enclosed within a high **boundary wall** (Prakara), and the **Gopurams** serve as the grand entry points into these enclosures.
 
• The main tower over the sanctum is called the **Vimana**, which is shaped like a **stepped pyramid** that rises geometrically, distinguishing it from the curved towers of Northern styles.
 
• Other essential elements of this architecture include a temple tank known as the **Kalyani** or **Pushkarni** and a pillared hall called the **Mandapa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara style**:

 
 
• Prevalent in **North India**, this style is characterized by the absence of elaborate boundary walls and **Gopurams**.
 
• The primary feature is the **Shikhara**, a curvilinear tower that rises over the **Garbhagriha** (sanctum sanctorum).
 
 
 
• **Vesara style**:
 
 
• A **hybrid style** that originated in the **Deccan** region under the **Western Chalukyas** and **Hoysalas**.
 
• It incorporates elements from both **Nagara** and **Dravidian** styles, often featuring a **star-shaped** base and a fusion of tower designs.
 
 
 
• **Pala style**:
 
 
• Developed in the **Bengal** and **Bihar** regions between the **8th and 12th centuries**.
 
• It is known for the extensive use of **terracotta** and **burnt bricks**, with temple shapes often influenced by local thatched bamboo huts.

questions.question: Selected for the International Space Station mission in 2025, John McFall, the first disabled astronaut, is associated with which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Kingdom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John McFall** is a **British** citizen and a former **Paralympic sprinter** who has been selected for a pioneering mission to the **International Space Station (ISS)**.
 
• He was selected by the **European Space Agency (ESA)** in **November 2022** as the world’s first **parastronaut**, a term used for an astronaut with a physical disability.
 
• As part of the **'Fly!' feasibility study**, McFall is working with **ESA** and its international partners to evaluate the technical, safety, and functional requirements for a person with a physical disability to live and work in microgravity.
 
• The mission, anticipated around **2025**, aims to demonstrate that space exploration can be inclusive, making the **United Kingdom** a leader in the evolution of human spaceflight criteria.
 
• His selection followed a rigorous process involving over **22,500 applicants**, highlighting the shift in space agencies toward broader human diversity in space missions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biographical Background**:

 
 
• **John McFall** lost his right leg in a motorcycle accident at the age of **19** and later became a professional athlete, winning a **Bronze medal** in the **100m** at the **2008 Beijing Paralympic Games**.
 
• In addition to his athletic achievements, he is a highly qualified **orthopedic surgeon**, holding a medical degree from **Cardiff University** and being a member of the **Royal College of Surgeons**.
 
 
 
• **International Space Agency Context**:
 
 
• **ESA (European Space Agency)**: Headquartered in **Paris**, it represents **22 member states**, including the **United Kingdom**. The **UK Space Agency** funds the UK’s involvement in **ESA** programs.

questions.question: Razia, the daughter of Iltutmish, ruled Delhi Sultanate between which years before being overthrown by Turkish nobles?

• **Razia Sultan**, the daughter of **Shamsuddin Iltutmish**, ascended the throne of the **Delhi Sultanate** in **1236**, becoming the first female Muslim ruler in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: The S.I. derived unit for **Force** is the Newton (N). Which combination of S.I. base units is equivalent to the Newton?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg⋅m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Force** is fundamentally defined by **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, which states that the force applied to an object is the product of its **mass** and its **acceleration** (F = m × a).
 
• The **S.I. base unit** for **mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**, which is one of the seven fundamental units of the **International System of Units**.
 
• **Acceleration** is a **derived quantity** defined as the rate of change of **velocity** over **time**. Since velocity is measured in **meters per second (m/s)** and time is measured in **seconds (s)**, the unit for acceleration is **m/s²**.
 
• By substituting these base units into the physical formula, the unit for **Force** becomes **kg × m/s²**, which is collectively termed the **Newton (N)**.
 
• One **Newton** is defined as the amount of force required to accelerate a mass of one **kilogram** at a rate of one **meter per second squared** (1 N = 1 kg⋅m/s²).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Linear Momentum**:

 
 
• The unit **kg⋅m/s** represents **Linear Momentum** (p = m × v), which describes the quantity of motion of a moving body.
 
 
 
• **Work and Energy**:
 
 
• The unit **kg⋅m²/s²** is the base unit equivalent of the **Joule (J)**, used to measure **Work** (Force × Displacement) and **Energy**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The **Newton** was named in honor of **Sir Isaac Newton**, whose **Principia Mathematica** (1687) laid the foundations for **classical mechanics**.
 
 
 
• **S.I. Base Units**:
 
 
• The system relies on seven base units, including the **meter (m)** for length, **kilogram (kg)** for mass, and **second (s)** for time, from which all other units like the **Newton**, **Pascal**, and **Watt** are derived.

questions.question: The roads and streets of the Harappan Lower Town were laid out in which pattern?

options.text: Grid pattern intersecting at right angles
Radial pattern spreading from a centre

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grid pattern intersecting at right angles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Harappan Civilization**, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, is renowned for its sophisticated urban planning and advanced engineering.
 
• The **Lower Town** of Harappan cities, such as **Mohenjo-daro** and **Harappa**, was characterized by a systematic arrangement where roads and streets were laid out in a **grid pattern**.
 
• The main streets were designed to be straight and broad, intersecting each other precisely at **right angles** (90 degrees), effectively dividing the residential areas into rectangular or square blocks.
 
• This **chessboard pattern** ensured efficient movement and reflected a high degree of administrative control and architectural foresight.
 
• The streets were integrated with an elaborate **drainage system**, where smaller drains from houses led into larger drains running alongside the main roads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Structure of Harappan Cities:**

 
 
• **Citadel:** A raised area on the western side, typically housing important public buildings like the **Great Bath** and the **Granary**.
 
• **Lower Town:** Located on the eastern side, this was the residential sector where common citizens lived, featuring houses made of **baked bricks**.
 
• **Standardization:** Unlike other contemporary civilizations, Harappan cities utilized **standardized burnt bricks** with a ratio of 1:2:4 for construction.
 
• **Drainage Technology:** Every house had its own bathroom and was connected to the street drains, which were covered with **stone slabs** or bricks for maintenance.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Patterns:**
 
 
• **Circular or Radial Patterns:** These layouts involve streets curving or branching out from a central point, which were not characteristic of Harappan planning.
 
• **Irregular Patterns:** These are found in unplanned settlements where growth is organic rather than pre-determined, the opposite of the highly organized **Indus Valley** sites.

questions.question: Which of the following trees is characteristic of the tropical deciduous forests of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Teak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests**, also known as **Monsoon Forests**, are the most widespread forest type in **India**, occupying regions that receive annual rainfall between **70 cm and 200 cm**.
 
• **Teak** (scientific name **Tectona grandis**) is the most dominant and characteristic tree species of these forests. It is highly valued for its durable and high-quality timber, used extensively in furniture making and construction.
 
• These forests are characterized by the seasonal shedding of leaves. The trees shed their foliage for about **six to eight weeks** during the **dry summer** to minimize water loss through transpiration.
 
• The distribution of **Teak** is concentrated in the **central parts of India**, the **Deccan Plateau**, the **eastern slopes of the Western Ghats**, and the **foothills of the Himalayas**.
 
• Tropical deciduous forests are further classified into **Moist Deciduous** (100−200 cm rainfall) and **Dry Deciduous** (70−100 cm rainfall), with **Teak** being a primary component of both, though it thrives best in the moist subtype.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mangrove**:

• Characterized by **pneumatophores** or breathing roots. Major examples include the **Sunderbans** in West Bengal, where **Sundari** trees are found.
 
 
 
• **Deodar**:
 
 
• A prominent species of the **Montane (Himalayan) Forests**, specifically found in the Western Himalayas.
 
• Grows at altitudes between **1,500 and 2,500 meters** and provides strong, aromatic timber used in structural work.
 
 
 
• **Fir**:
 
 
• A **coniferous** tree typical of the **Temperate and Alpine Forests** at higher altitudes in the **Himalayas**.
 
• Usually found at elevations above **2,500 meters**, where temperatures are significantly lower.
 
 
 
• **Other Deciduous Species**:
 
 
• In **Moist Deciduous Forests**, other important species include **Sal, Shisham, Hurra, Mahua, Amla, Semul, Kusum,** and **Sandalwood**.

questions.question: Which soil type, known for retaining moisture, is ideal for cotton cultivation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black soil**, also popularly known as **Regur soil** or **Black Cotton Soil**, is scientifically categorized as **Vertisols** due to its high clay content and unique expansive properties.
 
• The most defining characteristic of this soil is its exceptional **moisture retention capacity**; it swells and becomes sticky when wet, and develops deep wide cracks upon drying, which facilitates **self-aeration** or self-plowing.
 
• Geologically, it is derived from the **weathering of volcanic rocks** (Basalt) found in the **Deccan Trap** region, covering approximately **15%** of India total land area including **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, and parts of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It is chemically rich in minerals such as **calcium carbonate**, **magnesium**, **potash**, and **lime**, but generally lacks **phosphorus**, **nitrogen**, and **organic matter**.
 
• The soil is ideally suited for **cotton cultivation** because the crop requires sustained moisture levels throughout its growth cycle, which the deep clayey layers of black soil provide efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Soil Types:**

 
 
• **Laterite soil**:

 
 
• Formed through the process of **intense leaching** in regions with high temperatures and heavy seasonal rainfall.
 
• Rich in **iron oxide** and **aluminum**, it is primarily used for growing **cashew nuts**, **tea**, and **coffee**.
 
 
 
• **Red soil**:
 
 
• Develops on **crystalline igneous rocks** in areas of low rainfall in the eastern and southern parts of the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• Its reddish color is attributed to a wide diffusion of **iron** in crystalline and metamorphic rocks; it appears yellow when in **hydrated** form.
 
 
 
• **Sandy soil**:
 
 
• Consists of large particles with high **porosity**, leading to very low **water-holding capacity**.
 
• Mainly found in **arid and semi-arid** regions like **Rajasthan**, it is generally unsuitable for moisture-intensive crops like cotton.

questions.question: In modern Windows versions (Windows 10/11), which Task Manager tab allows users to monitor real-time graphics card utilization for individual applications?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Processes tab** in modern **Windows Task Manager** (introduced in **Windows 10 Version 1709**) provides a granular, real-time view of hardware resource consumption for every active software and system process.
 
• It features a dedicated **GPU column** that displays the percentage of the **Graphics Processing Unit** being utilized by **individual applications**, allowing users to identify which specific program is causing heavy graphical load.
 
• Adjacent to the GPU usage percentage, the **GPU Engine** column specifies which part of the hardware is being leveraged, such as **3D**, **Video Encode**, or **Video Decode**, for each running process.
 
• This tab is the primary tool for **troubleshooting performance bottlenecks** caused by specific background tasks or high-demand software like video editors and games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Performance Tab:**

 
 
• Provides high-level, **system-wide telemetry** and graphical data for the **CPU**, **RAM**, **Disk**, and **GPU**.
 
• While it displays **dedicated video memory** and **shared system memory** usage, it does not breakdown the utilization by specific application names.
 
 
 
• **App History Tab:**
 
 
• Displays cumulative resource usage (such as **CPU time** and **network data**) over a specific time period, typically 30 days.
 
• It primarily tracks **Universal Windows Platform (UWP)** applications and does not offer live per-app **GPU monitoring** for all software.
 
 
 
• **Startup Tab:**
 
 
• Lists applications that are configured to launch automatically when the user logs into **Windows**.
 
• Its main function is to monitor and manage **Startup impact** on the **BIOS boot time**, rather than real-time GPU utilization during active use.

questions.question: Which of the following temples is NOT a prime example of the Dravidian style of temple architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siddhesvara Mahadeva Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brihadeeswara Temple**, also known as **Rajarajeswaram**, is a classic example of **Dravidian architecture** located in **Thanjavur**, Tamil Nadu. Built by the **Chola** emperor **Raja Raja I** between **1003 and 1010 CE**, it features a massive 13-story **Vimana** (temple tower) that stands approximately 66 meters high.
 
• The **Shore Temple** at **Mahabalipuram** represents the structural phase of **Pallava architecture**. Constructed under **Narasimhavarman II** (Rajasimha) in the 8th century, it is one of the oldest structural stone temples in South India and a key **Dravidian** monument.
 
• The **Gangaikondacholapuram Temple** was built by **Rajendra I**, the son of Raja Raja I, to commemorate his victory over the Pala dynasty of Bengal. It follows the **Dravidian style** with a slightly concave **Vimana**, distinguishing it from the Thanjavur temple.
 
• **Siddhesvara Mahadeva Temple** (specifically the ones located in **Bhubaneswar, Odisha** or **Barakar, West Bengal**) is a prime example of the **Nagara style** of architecture. These temples are characterized by a **Rekha Deul** (curvilinear spire) and a **Jagamohana** (assembly hall), which are defining traits of the **Kalinga** school of North Indian architecture, not the Dravidian style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian Architecture Features:**

 
 
• The presence of high enclosure walls and magnificent gateway towers known as **Gopurams**.
 
• The main temple tower, called the **Vimana**, is a stepped pyramid that rises geometrically.
 
• The presence of a large **temple tank** (water reservoir) within the complex is a mandatory feature.
 
• The **Garbagriha** (sanctum sanctorum) is connected to the assembly hall via an **Antarala** (vestibule).
 
 
 
• **Nagara Architecture Features:**
 
 
• The entire temple is usually built on a stone platform with steps leading up to it.
 
• Unlike Dravidian temples, they typically do not have elaborate boundary walls or **Gopurams**.
 
• The tower is called a **Shikhara**, which is curvilinear in shape and topped by a stone disc called an **Amalaka** and a **Kalasha**.

questions.question: In human beings, the complete digestion of proteins results in the formation of which substances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amino acids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proteins** are complex nitrogenous macromolecules composed of long chains of **monomers** known as **amino acids**, which are linked together by **peptide bonds**.
 
• The digestion of proteins begins in the **stomach**, where the highly acidic environment created by **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** facilitates the activation of the enzyme **pepsin**. Pepsin breaks down the large protein molecules into smaller fragments called **proteoses** and **peptones**.
 
• The process continues in the **small intestine**, where the **pancreas** releases proteolytic enzymes, including **trypsin**, **chymotrypsin**, and **carboxypeptidases**, which further hydrolyze the peptides into **dipeptides**.
 
• The final stage occurs at the **brush border** of the small intestine, where the enzyme **dipeptidase** (found in the **succus entericus**) breaks the remaining dipeptides into individual, free **amino acids**.
 
• These **amino acids** represent the simplest form of proteins and are the final products that can be absorbed through the **intestinal mucosa** into the **bloodstream** for use in **growth**, **repair**, and **enzyme production**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glucose**:

 
 
• It is a **monosaccharide** and the primary end product of **carbohydrate** digestion.
 
• Complex carbohydrates like **starch** are broken down by **amylase** and **maltase** into glucose to provide immediate energy for **metabolic activities**.
 
 
 
• **Fatty acids and Glycerol**:
 
 
• These are the fundamental building blocks and end products of **fat (lipid)** digestion.
 
• **Bile salts** from the liver first **emulsify** fats, which are then chemically broken down by **lipase** enzymes into fatty acids and glycerol for absorption into the **lacteals** (lymphatic vessels).

questions.question: The members of the Railway Convention Committee are nominated by which of the following authorities of India?

options.text: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

__
 
• The **Railway Convention Committee (RCC)** is an **ad-hoc Parliamentary Committee** that is specifically constituted to review the financial arrangements between the **Railway Undertaking** and the **General Finances** of the government.
 
• The committee consists of a total of **18 members** of Parliament, drawn from both houses.
 
• The composition includes **12 members** from the **Lok Sabha** and **6 members** from the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** nominates the members representing the lower house, while the **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** nominates the members representing the upper house.
 
• The **Chairman** of the **Railway Convention Committee** is appointed by the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** from among the members of the committee.
 
• The formation of the committee is initiated by a **resolution** moved by the **Minister of Railways** in the **Lok Sabha**, which is subsequently concurred in by the **Rajya Sabha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions of the RCC:**

 
 
• The primary function is to determine the **rate of dividend** payable by the **Railways** to the **General Revenues**.
 
• It also examines various aspects of railway finances, such as the **Railway Development Fund** and the **Depreciation Reserve Fund**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• The committee owes its origin to the **Separation Convention of 1924** (Acworth Committee recommendation), which separated **Railway Finance** from **General Finance**.
 
• The first **Railway Convention Committee** in independent India was set up in **1949**.
 
 
 
• **Roles of Other Authorities:**
 
 
• **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:** While the Chairman nominates the **6 members** from the **Rajya Sabha**, the overall coordination and the appointment of the committee head lie with the **Speaker**.
 
• **President and Prime Minister:** Neither the **President of India** nor the **Prime Minister** has any constitutional or procedural role in the nomination of members to **Parliamentary Committees**, as these are legislative bodies independent of the executive for internal appointments.

questions.question: Which among the following kings from the early medieval period assumed the title "Gangaikonda"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajendra I** (reigned **1014−1044 CE**) was the son of the legendary Chola king **Rajaraja I** and is considered one of the greatest military conquerors in Indian history.
 
• He launched a daring military expedition to **North India** around **1022−1023 CE**, crossing the **Godavari** and reaching the banks of the **Ganges River**.

questions.question: As per the Indian Constitution, the Directive Principles of State Policy are ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-justiciable but fundamental in governance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are contained in **Part IV** of the **Indian Constitution**, spanning from **Article 36 to Article 51**.
 
• According to **Article 37**, the provisions of this part are **non-justiciable**, which means they are not **enforceable by any court**. Unlike **Fundamental Rights**, a citizen cannot sue the government for the non-fulfillment of these directives.
 
• Despite their non-justiciable nature, **Article 37** explicitly mandates that these principles are **fundamental in the governance** of the country, and it shall be the **duty of the State** to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• The core aim of **DPSP** is to create a **Welfare State** by ensuring **social and economic justice**, serving as a guide for the **Legislature** and the **Executive** in policy formulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Source and Influence**:

 
 
• The **DPSP** are borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** (which in turn took them from the **Spanish Constitution**).
 
• They are similar to the **Instrument of Instructions** mentioned in the **Government of India Act, 1935**.
 
 
 
• **Categorization**:
 
 
• **Socialistic Principles**: Aim at providing social and economic justice (e.g., **Article 38**, **Article 39**).
 
• **Gandhian Principles**: Based on the ideology of **Mahatma Gandhi** (e.g., **Article 40** regarding **Village Panchayats**).
 
• **Liberal-Intellectual Principles**: Based on liberalism (e.g., **Article 44** regarding **Uniform Civil Code**).
 
 
 
• **Legal Status**:
 
 
• In the **Minerva Mills Case (1980)**, the **Supreme Court** ruled that the **Indian Constitution** is founded on the bedrock of the **balance** between **Fundamental Rights** and **Directive Principles**.
 
• While **Fundamental Rights** establish **political democracy**, **DPSP** strive to establish **social and economic democracy**.

questions.question: The CPU mainly performs which of the following functions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Processing and control**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** is widely regarded as the **brain** of the computer, responsible for interpreting and executing most of the commands from the computer’s hardware and software.
 
• The **Control Unit (CU)** is a core component that manages and coordinates the activities of all other units. It directs the flow of data between the **processor**, **memory**, and **peripheral devices** by generating timing and control signals.
 
• The **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)** is the part of the CPU where actual data **processing** occurs. It performs fundamental **arithmetic operations** (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and **logical comparisons** (equal to, greater than, less than).
 
• The CPU operates through a cycle known as the **Instruction Cycle** or **Fetch-Decode-Execute cycle**, where it retrieves instructions from **RAM**, determines the required action, and carries out the task.
 
• The primary function of the CPU is to process input data into meaningful **information** while maintaining synchronized **control** over the entire system architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functional Units of a Computer**:

 
 
• **Input Unit**: Devices like the **keyboard** and **mouse** that feed raw data into the system.
 
• **Output Unit**: Devices like the **monitor** (display) and **printer** that present the processed results to the user.
 
• **Storage Unit**: This consists of **Primary Memory (RAM/ROM)** for immediate data access and **Secondary Storage (HDD/SSD)** for permanent data retention.
 
 
 
• **CPU Components**:
 
 
• **Registers**: Small, high-speed storage locations within the CPU used to hold instructions and data currently being processed.
 
• **Cache Memory**: A small amount of high-speed **SRAM** that sits between the CPU and the main memory to speed up data retrieval processes.
 
 
 
• **Clock Speed**: Measured in **Gigahertz (GHz)**, it determines the number of cycles a CPU can perform per second, directly impacting **processing power**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Petroleum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-renewable resources** are natural substances that exist in **finite quantities** and cannot be replaced or regenerated by natural processes within a short geological timeframe.
 
• **Petroleum**, commonly referred to as **crude oil**, is a **fossil fuel** composed primarily of **hydrocarbons** and other organic compounds.
 
• It was formed over **millions of years** from the remains of ancient marine organisms, such as **plankton** and **algae**, which were subjected to intense **heat and pressure** deep within the **Earth's crust**.
 
• Because the consumption rate of petroleum significantly exceeds its extremely slow rate of **natural formation**, it is classified as an **exhaustible resource**.
 
• Once extracted and consumed, these reserves are depleted forever, making them unsustainable for long-term energy security compared to renewable alternatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Renewable Energy Sources**:

 
 
• **Solar Energy**: Harvested using **photovoltaic cells** or solar thermal collectors, this energy originates from **nuclear fusion** in the **Sun** and is considered inexhaustible.
 
• **Wind Energy**: Generated by the **kinetic energy** of airflows caused by the **uneven heating** of the Earth's surface; it is a clean, perpetual resource.
 
• **Biomass**: Derived from **organic materials** like wood, agricultural crops, and animal waste. It is renewable because plants can be **regrown** in relatively short cycles.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Context**:
 
 
• The use of petroleum is a major contributor to **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** emissions, leading to the **greenhouse effect** and **climate change**.
 
• In contrast, renewable sources like wind and solar produce little to no **greenhouse gases** during operation, supporting global **decarbonization** efforts.

questions.question: Which of the following states accounts for about three-fourths of India's total jute production?

• The **Hooghly river belt** serves as the central hub for the jute industry, offering the necessary **hot and humid climate** with temperatures between 24°C and 35°C and annual rainfall exceeding 150 cm.
 
• Processing jute requires an immense amount of **clean soft water** for **retting** (the process of soaking stalks to separate fibers), which is abundantly supplied by the river systems in the state.
 
• The availability of **skilled inexpensive labor** from neighboring regions and well-connected **waterway transportation** further supports the massive scale of cultivation and manufacturing in this region.

• **Odisha**: Production is mainly localized in coastal districts like **Cuttack**, **Puri**, and **Balasore**.

questions.question: In a cross between true-breeding red-flowered and true breeding white-flowered plants, the Filial 1 (F₁) progeny was pink. This is a case of which type of inheritance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Incomplete Dominance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Incomplete dominance** is a genetic phenomenon where the **dominant allele** does not completely mask the effects of a **recessive allele**, resulting in a **blended phenotype** in the heterozygote.
 
• In the cross described, the **true-breeding red-flowered plant** (genotype RR) and the **true-breeding white-flowered plant** (genotype rr) produce **F₁ progeny** with the genotype Rr.
 
• The **pink phenotype** observed in the **F₁ generation** is an **intermediate expression** between red and white, which characterizes **incomplete dominance**.
 
• This pattern of inheritance was famously observed by **Carl Correns** in **Mirabilis jalapa** (Four o clock plant) and is also seen in **Antirrhinum majus** (Snapdragon).
 
• In the **F₂ generation**, produced by selfing the F₁ hybrids, the **phenotypic ratio** and **genotypic ratio** are identical at **1:2:1** (1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Complete Dominance**:

 
 
• Occurs when the **dominant allele** completely covers up the **recessive allele** in the heterozygous state.
 
• The **F₁ phenotype** is identical to the dominant parent, as seen in **Mendel’s pea plant** experiments (e.g., Tall vs. Dwarf).
 
 
 
• **Co-dominance**:
 
 
• A condition where **both alleles** are simultaneously and equally expressed in the **heterozygote** without blending.
 
• Classic examples include the **ABO blood group** (specifically the AB type) and **sickle-cell trait**.
 
 
 
• **Sex-linkage**:
 
 
• Refers to the inheritance of genes located on the **sex chromosomes** (X or Y).
 
• Traits like **Haemophilia** and **Red-green color blindness** follow this pattern, often showing **criss-cross inheritance**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presiding over Rajya Sabha sessions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 64** and **Article 89** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Vice-President of India** serves as the **ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States). It is the **Vice-President**, not the **President**, who is responsible for **presiding over Rajya Sabha sessions**, maintaining order, and regulating the business of the house. Hence, statement 3 is the correct identification of what is NOT a presidential function.
 
• The **President** is empowered by **Article 72** to grant **pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions** of punishment or to suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence in specific cases, such as court-martial or death sentences. Hence, statement 1 is a function of the President.
 
• According to **Article 123**, the **President** has the legislative power to **promulgate ordinances** during the recess of **Parliament**. These ordinances have the same force and effect as an **Act of Parliament** but must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of its reassembly. Hence, statement 2 is a function of the President.
 
• **Article 85** mandates that the **President** shall from time to time **summon** each House of **Parliament** to meet. The President also has the authority to **prorogue** the Houses and **dissolve the Lok Sabha**. Hence, statement 4 is a function of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Role of the Vice-President**

 
 
• The **Vice-President** acts as the **President** during a vacancy caused by death, resignation, or removal, but otherwise performs the primary function of **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha**.
 
• While presiding, the **Vice-President** does not have a vote in the first instance but holds a **casting vote** in case of an equality of votes.
 
 
 
• **Executive and Legislative Powers of the President**
 
 
• The **President** is the **Supreme Commander** of the **Defence Forces** of India.
 
• All **executive actions** of the **Government of India** are formally taken in the name of the **President**.
 
• The **President** appoints the **Prime Minister**, other Ministers, the **Attorney General**, and **Governors of States**.
 
• A **bill** passed by **Parliament** becomes an **Act** only after receiving the **Presidential assent** under **Article 111**.

questions.question: When a book is pushed across a table surface, which type of friction mainly opposes its motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sliding friction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sliding friction**, also referred to as **kinetic friction**, is the resistive force that acts between two solid surfaces when one is sliding over the other.
 
• When a **book** is pushed across a **table**, the physical contact between the two surfaces results in the interlocking of **microscopic irregularities** (projections and depressions), which opposes the **relative motion**.
 
• The direction of this frictional force is always **parallel** to the contact surfaces and **opposite** to the direction of the applied force or motion.
 
• The magnitude of sliding friction is determined by the **coefficient of kinetic friction** (μₖ) and the **normal force** (N), expressed as fₖ = μₖN.
 
• It is a **non-conservative force**, meaning it dissipates **kinetic energy** into **thermal energy** (heat), which is why surfaces often warm up when rubbed together.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rolling friction**:

 
 
• Occurs when a spherical or cylindrical object, such as a **ball**, **wheel**, or **roller**, rolls over a surface.
 
• It is significantly **weaker** than sliding friction because the area of contact is minimal, making it easier to move heavy loads using **wheels** or **ball bearings**.
 
 
 
• **Fluid friction**:
 
 
• Also known as **viscous drag**, this is the resistance encountered by objects moving through **fluids** (liquids or gases).
 
• It depends on the **viscosity** of the medium, the **shape** of the object (streamlining), and the **speed** of motion.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic friction**:
 
 
• Refers to **electromagnetic braking** or **eddy current damping**, where motion is resisted by **magnetic fields** and induced currents.
 
• It does not require physical contact between surfaces and is used in modern **high-speed trains** and **gym equipment**.

questions.question: What does CD stand for in computer terminology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compact Disc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Compact Disc** is a digital **optical disc** data storage format that was co-developed by **Sony** and **Philips**, officially hitting the market in **1982**.
 
• The technology utilizes a **semiconductor laser** with a wavelength of approximately **780 nanometers** to read data stored as microscopic **pits** and **lands** on a spiral track.
 
• Standard CDs have a physical diameter of **120 millimeters** and a thickness of **1.2 millimeters**, providing a storage capacity of **700 MB** or about **80 minutes** of uncompressed **Pulse Code Modulation (PCM)** audio.
 
• Structurally, a CD consists of a **polycarbonate plastic** substrate, a thin **reflective layer** (usually aluminum), and a protective **lacquer** coating to prevent oxidation and physical damage.
 
• In computer terminology, the **CD-ROM** (Read-Only Memory) standard was established in the **Yellow Book** (1985), allowing discs to store computer data rather than just audio.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variations of CD Technology**:

 
 
• **CD-R (Compact Disc-Recordable)**: Uses a **photosensitive organic dye** layer that allows a laser to **burn** data onto the disc once.
 
• **CD-RW (Compact Disc ReWritable)**: Employs a **phase-change** alloy (typically silver, indium, antimony, and tellurium) that can be melted and recrystallized to erase and rewrite data multiple times.
 
• **VCD (Video Compact Disc)**: A format for storing video on a CD using **MPEG-1** compression, popular before the advent of DVDs.
 
 
 
• **Distinction from Software Commands**:
 
 
• The acronym **cd** in a **Command Line Interface (CLI)** like Windows Command Prompt or Linux Terminal stands for **Change Directory**, which is used to navigate between different folders in a file system.
 
 
 
• **Successor Technologies**:
 
 
• **DVD (Digital Versatile Disc)**: Introduced in **1995**, offering **4.7 GB** storage using a **650 nm** red laser.
 
• **Blu-ray Disc**: Uses a **405 nm** blue-violet laser to achieve capacities of **25 GB** or more per layer.
